newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch signals delays to foreign tax reform.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch signals delays to foreign tax reform.

text.p: Revenue Minister Bill Birch on Friday signalled further delays in reforming international tax issues.

In a speech to the International Fiscal Association Birch said the National-New Zealand First coalition government did not want a tax system which deterred or distorted investment, but some issues were proving difficult.

He singled out as unfair and leading to double taxation the "conduit" problem, which penalises overseas investors who use New Zealand subsidiaries to invest offshore, and the "triangular" problem where a New Zealand shareholder in an
Australian company earning dividends from New Zealand activities does not receive imputation credits on tax paid.
The previous National government had set December for the release of a discussion document on the conduit problem, but this was postponed until March.

"We've reached March. It's not just a question here of getting a new government up to speed. A genuine solution would be unusually knotty, with major trade-offs to evaluate between conduit relief and tax base protection," Birch said.
After discussion last year between Birch and Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, work began on solutions to the triangular problem.
Birch said the deadline for officials to report back was almost up, but they were still deep in discussions searching for practicable solutions.

Birch said taxing life and superannuation fund savings at 33 percent was also visibly unfair on low and middle income earners (whose tax rate is lower) and a joint private-public sector working party would probably report back before the end of March, Birch said.
He said he hoped to report by the end of March on progress on the three year policy work programme the government was formulating on tax.
